text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Poland's Constitutional Tribunal has declared illegal the regulation introduced late in 1995 which taxed the financially successful municipalities already in 1996. The issue will soon be re-examined by parliament.

- The Gdansk provinacial court has issued an arrest warrant for the Australian Brewpole PTY representative Tony Oates, charged with embezzlement by Australia's prosecutor general who demanded Oates' extradition.

- The Bielsko-Biala-based Fiat plant will start producing the Fiat Palio passenger car in May 1997. The new model will be sold as of September next year and will cost around $11,000, Fiat Auto Poland president Diego Avesani said.

- The EU motor industry experts will soon produce their opinion on car assemblying plants operating in Poland following their inspection in selected plants, deputy industry minister Tadeusz Soroka said.
- The Kedzierzyn-based Zaklady Azotowe Kedzierzyn fertilizer maker will invest 650 million zlotys in modernisation and technological development by 2000.

- The three-day Baltic Economic Forum will start in Sopot on October 24. The representatives of Russia's 100 regions as well as government officials will take part in the conference, the Russian embassy said. Inter-city cooperation between Poland's Gdynia and Russia's Rybinsk and a bus production joint-venture in Kaliningrad will be discussed at the Forum.
NOWA EUROPA
- A record number of 800,000 subscribers will recieve telephones by the year-end.

- The state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank, has reported a gross profit of 348.4 million zlotys in the first nine months of 1996, BGZ financial department Michal Fogtman said.

- More than 70 companies are exhibiting alarm system products and mechanical protection devices for cars at the Garda'96 Protection System Exhibition organised by the Mokotow trading centre in Warsaw.

- The province governors of western Poland have initiated the Wielkopolska Rada Gospodarcza (WRG) regional economic council which groups 41 businessmen and economic experts. The new advisory and opinion making body and will promote the region's economic development.
- Over 70 forwarding firms are participating in the "Cargoterns'96" international transport and forwarding fair in Szczecin, northwestern Poland.
- Germany's Kludi Group has opened a sanitary fittings plant which cost 20 million zlotys to build.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Polish construction firms will find it easier to operate in Germany as the result of agreements made during the Polish-German talks held in Krakow this week.
- Despite Poland's poor grain harvests this year, good harvests around the world will stabilise Poland's market through cheap imports, agricultural economy institute experts said.
- The Szczecin-based Espebepe construction firm will carry out a construction contract in Berlin worth DM 1 million.
- The BGZ bank has contracted Mostostal Warszawa construction company to carry out adaptation and extension works at the bank's central office worth 50 million zlotys.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY

- Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) environment protection and construction department has started the Warsaw metro project control. "We have no reasons to fear the results of the control", the Metro project chief engineer Kalina Jaworska said.
PARKIET
- Mostostal Warszawa will carry out two construction projects for Poland's Post Office in Warsaw worth 20 million zlotys, the Mostostal management said.
- In accordance with the corporate sector privatisation and commercialisation regulations, the employees of four listed companies will receive free shares worth 202 million zlotys.
- Kredyt Bank has acquired 2,800 shares in the PolCard Ltd. credit card firm, worth 280,000 zlotys. The bank now holds an 11.03 percent stake in the company.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
